data.name: Indonesia
data.summary: Indonesia taxes residents on worldwide income at up to 35%. That rate applies to gains on foreign shares and to foreign dividends, unless the reinvestment-in-Indonesia exemptions apply. Indonesian listed shares bear only a 0.1% tax on sale proceeds, and Indonesian dividends a 10% final tax. Foreign experts can be taxed only on Indonesian income for four years, but that needs qualifying work. There is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. A golden visa exists for large investors (thresholds not verified).

regimes.name: Indonesian tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation at 5%-35%; final taxes on IDX share sales, Indonesian dividends and Indonesian property.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if residing in Indonesia, present more than 183 days in any 12 months, or present in a year with intent to reside.

capital_gains.summary: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Capital gains are ordinary income at the progressive rates (5%-35%; 35% above IDR 5 billion), except sales of shares on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (0.1% final tax on proceeds) and transfers of land and buildings (2.5% final tax on the gross transfer value). Gains on foreign listed shares are therefore taxed at up to 35%, with a foreign tax credit.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: None for securities. Gains from mutual funds are exempt (PwC).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Foreign experts who become resident may elect to be taxed only on Indonesian-source income for their first four years (Omnibus Law; special regime, needs qualifying skills). Founder shares on IPO: optional 0.5% on listing value.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign shares, private company shares and foreign property: top progressive rate 35%. Proceeds-based final taxes converted to a rate on the gain assuming the gain is half of the proceeds: IDX shares 0.1% of proceeds -> 0.2% of the gain; Indonesian land and buildings 2.5% of gross value -> 5% of the gain.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading as a business is taxed as business income at progressive rates; IDX sales remain under the 0.1% final tax.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation with credit for foreign tax (per-country limit; not detailed by PwC).

dividends.summary: Dividends from Indonesian companies bear a 10% final tax, or none if the resident individual reinvests them in Indonesia within the prescribed period. Foreign dividends are taxed at the progressive rates up to 35% with credit for foreign tax, unless they qualify for the reinvestment exemption for foreign dividends introduced by the 2020/2021 tax laws (not verified).
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign dividends: exemption if invested in Indonesia within a set period (for listed foreign companies the dividend itself; for unlisted, at least 30% of after-tax profit) under the Omnibus/HPP amendments to Income Tax Law Art. 4(3) (general knowledge, not verified).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land and buildings tax (PBB) annually at up to 0.5% of the government-determined value; BPHTB acquisition duty up to 5% on purchases; 2.5% final tax for the seller.

inheritance.summary: Indonesia has no inheritance, estate or gift tax. Property acquired by gift is exempt income for the recipient (PwC lists it as exempt; under the Income Tax Law the exclusion covers gifts between direct-line relatives of one degree), and undivided inheritances are not income. The heir pays land and building acquisition duty (BPHTB, up to 5% above a regional threshold that starts at IDR 300 million for inheritances) on Indonesian real estate.
inheritance.important_exceptions: BPHTB on inherited Indonesian property is not reflected in other_transfer_cost_rate because the family's estate is mostly securities; foreigners can hold only use rights (Hak Pakai) to land.

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; gifts to children are excluded from the recipient's income. BPHTB up to 5% applies to transfers of Indonesian land and buildings, including by gift and inheritance.

income.name: Indonesia

income_tax.summary: Residents pay 5% to 35% on taxable income after IDR 54 million personal relief and a 5% occupational expense deduction (max IDR 6 million a year). Residents are taxed on worldwide income; only certified foreign experts get a four-year territorial treatment. Employees pay about 4% to BPJS.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Employee shares (PwC Indonesia other-taxes page: old-age savings 2%, pension 1%, BPJS Kesehatan 1%; employer-only: work accident, death, unemployment): BPJS Kesehatan 1% (calculation base capped at IDR 12 million a month), old-age savings 2%, pension 1% (capped, figure not on page). Because the health cap is monthly while the other bases are not capped on the page, the blended 4% overstates burden at high incomes. Self-employed contributions were not covered on the PwC page; whether foreigners without an Indonesian employer must enrol was not verified.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No national local income tax. Personal relief for a single taxpayer is IDR 54 million, plus IDR 4.5 million for a spouse and each dependant (up to three). Bali has no extra income tax.

regimes.name: Remote Worker Visa (E33G)
regimes.description: One-year ITAS for remote workers with a contract with a company established outside Indonesia, income of about USD 60,000 a year and USD 2,000 in liquid funds. Renewable once (two years maximum). It gives no tax exemption: holders become tax residents early (permit over 183 days counts as intent to reside under PER-23/PJ/2025) and are taxed on worldwide income. The Bali immigration office (Kantor Imigrasi Ngurah Rai) press release of 28 September 2026 on the immigration site shows an 'ITAS Remote Worker' exists in practice.
regimes.duration_note: Initial 1-year ITAS, one renewal. Earning from Indonesian entities or customers is prohibited. Fee reported around IDR 7,000,000 but inconsistent.

regimes.name: Four-year territorial treatment for certified foreign experts (PP 55/2022)
regimes.description: Under the Omnibus Law a foreigner who becomes tax resident and meets skill requirements is taxed only on Indonesian-source income (including income paid offshore) for the first four years of residence. A secondary source says it is limited to certified specified expertise in science, technology or mathematics with at least five years of experience and a knowledge-transfer obligation, so ordinary employees and remote workers usually do not qualify. Not available where a tax treaty is used. Indonesian-source income, including pay for work done in Indonesia, stays taxable; only income from outside Indonesia is relieved.
regimes.duration_note: First four years of tax residence.

succession.name: Indonesia
succession.summary: Which law applies depends on religion and community. Under the Civil Code, children and parents have a protected share; Muslims follow Islamic fixed shares and can will at most one third. A foreigner's movables follow their national law but a foreigner cannot hold Indonesian freehold land, and Indonesia has no trust law and has not joined the Hague Trusts Convention.
succession.reserved_share: Civil Code (non-Muslims): children, legitime portie of one half of their intestate share with one child, two thirds with two, three quarters with three or more (art. 914); parents one half (art. 915). Muslims: Compilation of Islamic Law (Inpres 1/1991) fixed shares, with bequests limited to one third (art. 195).
succession.foreign_law_note: The Algemene Bepalingen (AB) arts. 16-17 apply personal-status law by nationality to foreigners and the law of the place for immovables, so a foreigner's movables follow their national law. Foreigners cannot own land (hak milik) under the Agrarian Law and Indonesian courts may apply public policy. Customary (adat) law also applies to some groups.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. Indonesia has no trust law; Law 42/1999 covers only fiduciary security. Foreign trusts are not clearly recognised and there is no special trust tax regime. Foundations (yayasan) are under Law 16/2001 as amended by Law 28/2004; they must pursue social, religious or humanitarian aims, and founders cannot take profit.
open_questions: Confirm Civil Code arts. 913-915 fractions from the official text; I used the standard legitime portie figures and the source retrieved did not quote them.

Confirm tax treatment of foreign trust distributions to Indonesian residents.

immigration.name: Indonesia
immigration.summary: No free movement for EU citizens; EU, US and other passports use the same routes. Investors can buy a 5- or 10-year Golden Visa (USD 350,000 in government bonds, or a USD 2.5 million company), or take a Second Home Visa (IDR 2 billion, about USD 130,000, no work). Remote workers (E33G) need about USD 60,000 a year. Retirees need a pension of about USD 3,000 a month. Most official pages could not be opened; figures come from Fragomen, EY, ASEAN Briefing and consultancies.
immigration.naturalisation: Citizenship by naturalisation under Law 12/2006 is understood to need age 18+, 5 consecutive years (or 10 non-consecutive) of legal residence, Indonesian language and presidential approval; not confirmed from an official page in this run.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Indonesia does not allow dual citizenship for adults (limited dual nationality for some children); not verified from an official page in this run.

routes.name: Golden Visa (individual, passive investment route)
routes.summary: Five or ten years of residence for buying Indonesian government bonds worth USD 350,000 to USD 700,000 (secondary sources add listed shares and bank deposits).
routes.requirements: Golden Visa (launched 25 October 2023; first announced 7 September 2023) gives 5 or 10 years of residence with no extra stay or work permits. Individuals: USD 350,000 (5 years) or USD 700,000 (10 years) in Indonesian government bonds; secondary guides also list IDX-listed shares, mutual funds or state-bank deposits and a property route at USD 1 million for 10 years. Not confirmed against the Directorate General of Immigration regulation.
routes.investment_options: USD 350,000 for 5 years; USD 700,000 for 10 years (bonds). Other asset classes per secondary guides, unverified.
routes.family: Spouse and children on dependant stay permits (details not verified).
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day test; a stay permit longer than 183 days may be treated as intent to reside (per a 2026 tax guide, PER-23/PJ/2025, unverified).

routes.requirements: Golden Visa (launched 25 October 2023; first announced 7 September 2023) gives 5 or 10 years of residence with no extra stay or work permits. Corporate route for directors and commissioners: USD 25 million (5 years) or USD 50 million (10 years). routes.name: Second Home Visa (Rumah Kedua)
routes.summary: Five or ten years of residence without the right to work, for people who show IDR 2 billion (about USD 130,000) in an Indonesian state bank or own qualifying property.
routes.requirements: Show about IDR 2 billion (USD 130,000) in an individual account at an authorised Indonesian (state-owned per some sources) bank, or property: reports differ (USD 1 million apartment per EY, or Hak Pakai property of IDR 5 billion / apartment of IDR 2 billion per a Bali consultancy). Proof within 90 days or the stay permit is cancelled (secondary). No work allowed. After 3 years may move to a permanent permit (KITAP) per ASEAN Briefing.
routes.investment_options: IDR 2 billion bank balance; or property per conflicting figures.
routes.tax_note: A stay permit over 183 days may make you an Indonesian tax resident.
